verdict.rationale: Greptile's security page says customers can turn off logging to make chats private, and that self-hosted logs stay on customer servers. That is a first-party control close to opting out of usage tracking. However, the same page reserves the right to aggregate and anonymize customer data for analytics and AI training, with no documented opt-out. missing for 10: an explicit telemetry/usage-analytics opt-out setting, an opt-out from de-identified analytics and AI training, documentation of how to disable it, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can opt out of telemetry and usage tracking

citations.quote: Customers can choose to turn off logging and make chats 100% private.
Note that in the self-hosted service, logs are stored on customer servers only.
